shortDescription: By Junko FujitaJapanese government bond yields fell on Wednesday, tracking declines in global bond yields, even after a dovish Bank of Japan policymaker backed further interest rate increases.

children: Japanese government bond yields fell on Wednesday, tracking declines in global bond yields, even after a dovish Bank of Japan policymaker backed further interest rate increases.
The benchmark 10-year JGB yield (JP10YTN=JBTC) fell 1 basis point (bp) to 3.085%. Yields move inversely to bond prices
US Treasuries rebounded on Tuesday after a sharp selloff in the previous session pushed long-term yields to multi-decade highs
New BOJ policymaker Ayano Sato said she supports raising rates in several stages, the Kyodo news agency reported
Sato was one of two dissenters when the central bank raised rates in September
"The remarks from Sato are not going to affect the overall direction of the BOJ," said Shuichi Ohsaki, senior portfolio manager at Meiji Yasuda Asset Management
"As Japanese political leaders have moved away from the reflationary approach, Sato has changed her stance to be in line with the direction," said Ohsaki
Katsutoshi Inadome, senior strategist at Sumitomo Mitsui Trust Asset Management, said the market struggled to assess her comments
"Some may have thought Sato was not as dovish as they had thought; some may not," he said
Inadome said investors were split on how Bank of Japan rate hikes would affect the market

"Theoretically, if the BOJ raises rates, the 10-year bond yield would rise. But the yield could fall if the rate hike reduces concern about the central bank being behind the curve in coping with rising prices," he said
The two-year yield (JP2YTN=JBTC) inched down 0.5 bp to 1.92%
The five-year yield (JP5YTN=JBTC) was flat at 2.390%
